**Native HTML forms need both `method='POST'` AND `action='/path'`.** A form with no action posts to the current URL - `/signup.html` 404s because the framework's signup endpoint is `/signup` (no `.html`). Always set the action attribute explicitly.

**Don't write a `_csrf` field** in a page form. The runtime adds one to every POST or HTMX hx-post/put/patch/delete form it serves (static/ HTML and server-rendered pages); a GET form (method="get", no method, hx-get) gets none, so the token never lands in a URL. A hand-written field doesn't help: in mustache `{{csrf}}` renders empty, in gotmpl `{{.csrf}}` renders empty (`{{csrf}}` is a helper that writes the hidden input and meta tag itself, so place it inside the form, not in a value attribute), and in static/ HTML a field you write stops the runtime adding the real one.

**The runtime auto-injects the hidden `_csrf` input** into every native POST form in served static HTML (mirrors the meta tag injection). Symptom of the missing field: form submits redirect to `?error=Invalid+request` and the user sees no obvious feedback.

Tokens are signed with the app's server secret. Hosted apps have a stable per-instance `BENMORE_SERVER_SECRET`, so a restart, deploy or reload keeps tokens valid; a self-hosted `benmore serve` without one (32+ characters) generates a secret per process, and a restart then makes old tokens fail with 403 `Invalid CSRF token` (the server log line reads `validateCSRF: REJECT ... reason=hmac_mismatch`) - reload the page or GET /api/_csrf for a fresh token.
Tokens are valid for exactly 24h after issuance.
Bearer-auth (Authorization: Bearer …) is exempt - no cookie to abuse.

Besides the token, a cookie-authenticated mutation must come from the app's own origin: an Origin header naming another host, or Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site / same-site without one, is refused. A page whose referrer policy is `no-referrer` (a `<meta name="referrer">` tag or the header) makes the browser send `Origin: null` on its classic form POSTs even to its own origin; that is accepted only together with `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`. Prefer `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` on pages that post forms; fetch() calls are not affected.
